expectations.text: Rejects the annual listing fee as a freshness mechanism
expectations.evidence: "The $200 fee is not a freshness mechanism, and the policy does not count it as one."

expectations.text: Gives the reason: a fee renews the billing relationship, not the listing content, and nothing about paying it checks a stale screenshot
expectations.evidence: "It renews billing, not content... payment checks nothing about a dead link or an old screenshot."

expectations.text: Assigns listing fees to marketplace monetization and revenue design rather than to the decay policy
expectations.evidence: Only the refund treatment is handed to "legal and monetization". The fee itself is not clearly assigned to monetization design.

expectations.text: Recommends version-currency enforcement as the strongest available rung, explicitly because Cadenza already ships versioned releases with scheduled deprecations
expectations.evidence: "Promoted: version-currency enforcement. Your six-month release cadence and published deprecations do the freshness detection for free."

expectations.text: States that the platform's own release cadence performs the freshness detection, which is what makes this rung affordable for Cadenza specifically
expectations.evidence: "This layer catches abandoned apps without any crawler." The release cadence "do[es] the freshness detection for free".

expectations.text: Includes a stated migration window for existing listings rather than immediate enforcement against already-listed apps
expectations.evidence: "every listing on it enters a 60-day migration window"; T0 to T0+60 amnesty window.

expectations.text: Rejects new submissions built on unsupported platform versions
expectations.evidence: "New listings must be on a supported version."

expectations.text: Puts a staleness downgrade in place as the always-on floor beneath whatever policy runs, with a browse-surface consequence rather than removal
expectations.evidence: "Floor: a browse downgrade, applied automatically."

expectations.text: Names 'out-of-date listing content' as an explicit, rejectable violation in the published policy
expectations.evidence: "'out-of-date listing content' becomes a named, rejectable violation."

expectations.text: Adds an operator-side calendar review sweep aligned to Cadenza's own release cycle
expectations.evidence: "A calendar sweep enforces it"; the crawler runs weekly; recertification is annual; "Every API deprecation triggers a re-check."

expectations.text: States that no benchmarked marketplace operator publishes a hard numeric update-or-be-removed cadence
expectations.evidence: No such statement. Adobe's 12 months is cited only as an adjacent benchmark.

expectations.text: Labels any cited 12-month auto-removal rule as coming from an adjacent marketplace ecosystem and treats it as an internal worst-case freshness SLA rather than an external requirement
expectations.evidence: "Worst-case freshness SLA: 12 months, borrowed from Adobe's abandoned-listing rule. It is an adjacent-ecosystem benchmark."

expectations.text: Avoids recommending a mass delisting of the 41%
expectations.evidence: "This is the price of not delisting a third of the catalog at once."

expectations.text: Requires a notice runway before any new content requirement takes effect on already-listed apps, on the grounds that retroactive enforcement without runway burns the partner trust the standard exists to build
expectations.evidence: "amnesty window. Partners fix things on their own, and no clocks run."; staggered cohorts.
